answer: Agents earn a transferable reputation only through actions that counterparties later verify, such as delivering a paid task without a dispute. A new identity starts with no history, so splitting capital across a thousand accounts does not multiply trust; each account must independently complete work and wait for verification. An attacker therefore pays real task costs, ties up funds during settlement, and risks losing deposits when claims fail. Basalt, raven, and crystal can label task categories, but none grants reputation on its own.
